problems.form_value: Coded as contrasts of the randomized arms inside S2 (online_rct, randomized yes): 'AI-assisted (1-plot and 5-plot combined, as the paper labels it)' versus 'Human-only (0-plot, as the paper labels it)', ai_vs_bau; and 5-plot versus 1-plot, ai_design. The form flags the group-size conflict in open_questions and in the eligibility reason, but keeps this arm coding.
problems.source_says: The prose says the groups are the conditions (p. 12; p. 15), but the paper's own printed statistics show they are not the assigned arms. In Table 5 the six count-variable means come from whole-number totals only with 41 'Human' and 56 'AI-assisted' stories (the only split that sums to 97), and in Table 6 only with 27 1-plot and 29 5-plot stories. Example: Named Characters, Human mean 0.634 = 26/41, which no total over 32 stories gives (20/32 = 0.625, 21/32 = 0.656). AI-assisted mean 0.946 = 53/56, which no total over 65 gives (61/65 = 0.938, 62/65 = 0.954). Pooled two-sample t with 41/56 and 27/29 reproduces all 14 printed t values within 0.001. With the assigned 32/65 and 33/32 it reproduces none (for example Descriptive Words -2.331, printed -2.434). The Table 6 means, weighted 27/29, equal the Table 5 AI-assisted means. The NLTK step ran on the 97 analyzed stories (p. 52), of which 32 are controls (p. 11; Table 3), so 9 stories from the AI arms sit in the 'Human' group (6 from 1-plot and 3 from 5-plot, if the Table 6 groups are subsets of those arms). The paper never says why. The most likely rule is whether the writer requested a plot, which participants chose. Table S3 labels its block 'Originally Assigned Conditions', which fits a second, non-assigned grouping elsewhere. These 14 contrasts are not randomized comparisons. Under codebook section 4 (design coded per estimate) they belong to observational, and they should not enter the atlas as ai_vs_bau or ai_design estimates. The group sizes come from checker arithmetic: the paper prints no counts for Tables 5-6.

confirmed.statement: (a) The document states random assignment twice: 'The participants were randomly assigned to write an eight-sentence short story under one of three experimental conditions' and 'Each participant was randomly assigned to one of the three conditions'. The form's assignment quote is verbatim, and its locator is right.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Section 3.1 (the sentence continues on p. 11); p. 43, Supplementary Materials 'Story writing by participants'

confirmed.statement: Assignment is at the individual level and between person (unit individual, structure between). Each participant was assigned to one condition and wrote one story: 100 recruited, 3 excluded, 97 stories analyzed. There is no within-person design, so check (e) on the order of conditions does not apply.

(b) What was assigned is access to AI-generated material for the participant's own story: the option to request one plot idea (1-plot) or up to five (5-plot), against no AI support (0-plot). 'participants could choose whether to ask for plots or not, and were not required to use the plot ideas even if they requested them.' The conditions do not differ only in whose output gets evaluated: every S2 outcome is scored on the participant's own story.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Section 3.1; p. 43; interface screenshots pp. 45, 47-51

confirmed.statement: AI-arm participants 'received ideas randomly chosen from the diverse pool of 300 plot ideas generated by the 10 personas'. The interfaces match the arm descriptions: a 'Suggest Story Idea' button in 1-plot, five 'Idea' buttons in 5-plot, and the text 'You are free to use or disregard any element of the AI assistant's story idea'.

(c) The tool is generative AI. GPT-4o (version 2024-05-13, temperature 0.9, top P 1) on Azure OpenAI wrote the plots from 10 personas built with ChatGPT o1-preview. The pool was generated in Phase 1, before anyone wrote a story, so role ideas_supplied fits and the form's 'No live interaction with a model' is a fair reading.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 2.1; p. 30, Supplementary Materials 'Prompting the personas for plot ideas'; codebook section 6 (AI role)

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arms match the form. The 0-plot arm is 'write the story with no AI assistance' and its screen shows only the task, so 1-plot and 5-plot versus 0-plot are ai_vs_bau. 5-plot versus 1-plot is another AI configuration, which codebook section 5 lists as ai_design ('one idea versus five').
confirmed.locator: p. 43; p. 45 (0-plot screen); p. 10, Section 3.1; codebook section 5

confirmed.statement: participants.n_randomized 100 and n_analyzed 97 (32 / 33 / 32) are supported. Per-arm counts at assignment are not printed. By subtraction they are 35 / 33 / 32, because the only stated loss is 3 control stories and 97 stories 'remaining'. The form's null per-arm n_randomized is defensible.

The 3 exclusions came after randomization and from the control arm only (3 of 35, against 0 of 65 in the AI arms). They rest on a self-report question about ChatGPT use that the supplement shows only after the 0-plot condition. Table S3 calls its block 'Intent-to-Treat Analysis' but reports 'Achieved Power (n=97)'. The form records all of this, and none of it changes the assignment coding.

confirmed.statement: preregistered = not_stated is right. No preregistration, registry, OSF link or ethics statement appears in the 53 pages.
S1 (Phase 1) is correctly coded randomized = no and model only. 'Randomly sampled traits' describes how the personas were built, not the assignment of people.

Coverage: I read the whole markdown, which ends partway through the reference list (at Karimi et al.), and viewed PDF pp. 10-16 and 23-53 as page images, so the full supplement (pp. 28-53) was read from the PDF.

summary: Study S2 (Phase 2) is a between-person randomized experiment: the paper twice states that the 100 Prolific writers were randomly assigned to no AI or to the option of one or up to five GPT-4o persona plot ideas for their own story (p. 10; p. 43), and the diversity outcomes S2-O1 and S2-O2 compare those assigned arms (32 / 33 / 32 stories; 496 / 528 / 496 pairs, p. 13), so criterion 1 holds. The coding fails on one detail: the 14 NLTK contrasts from Tables 5-6 (S2-O3 to S2-O9) are coded as contrasts of the assigned arms, but the printed means and t values fit only groups of 41 vs 56 and 27 vs 29 stories, so 9 AI-arm stories sit in the 'Human' group and these contrasts are not randomized.
